characters.name: Darrow

world_facts.name: The Society
world_facts.description: A caste-based hierarchy categorized by colors, ranging from Red laborers to Gold rulers.

world_facts.name: Lykos
world_facts.description: A Red township on Mars where miners work to extract helium-3 to terraform the planet.

world_facts.name: Laureltide
world_facts.description: A celebration where the clan with the highest productivity receives the Laurel and extra rations.

world_facts.name: Dancer's Rebellion
world_facts.description: A failed peaceful protest led by Darrow's father, which ended in his execution on the gallows.

summary: Darrow, a young Red miner in the Lykos township, prepares for the annual Laureltide festival. While the Society’s propaganda displays the horrors of the 'Sons of Ares' rebellion on screens above, the residents of Lykos focus on their own survival and celebrations. Darrow, who has been working intensely to meet mining quotas, feels a sense of pride, believing he has secured the Laurel for his clan—a prestigious award that brings vital food rations and comforts. He navigates the festival alongside his wife, Eo, and his uncle, Narol, an embittered, alcoholic zither player who once taught him to dance. The atmosphere is thick with drink and music, yet overshadowed by the memory of the 'Devil’s Dance'—the execution of Darrow’s father for a failed rebellion. Tensions rise when Darrow and his uncle engage in a brief, violent brawl after Narol expresses disdain for Darrow's perceived arrogance. As the night progresses, Darrow remains hopeful, despite Eo’s strange and palpable apprehension about the outcome of the competition. At midnight, the MineMagistrate, Timony cu Podginus, descends from 'The Pot'—the elite fortress above—to announce the results. After a condescending speech about the misery of his own bureaucratic life, the Magistrate reveals the winners. Contrary to Darrow’s expectations and the silent hopes of his kin, the Laurel is awarded to the Gamma clan. Darrow is left to face the crushing reality that his efforts were insufficient, leaving his community in the familiar, bleak cycle of labor and scarcity while the ruling Golds maintain their total control over the resources of Mars.
